description: Canonical MSSR/SSR sensor-pipeline smoke test (v3.6.11). Verifies that selecting SSR in the Path Editor produces a working sensor end-to-end: build (via buildSensor -> buildRadar SSR path), classification (metadata 'type' tag routes to mssrBuffer, not heuristic fallback), beacon detection physics (Doppler/weather/clutter all auto-skip via ~si.isMSSR gates), tracker handoff (detections reach GNN+IMM, ObjectClassID stamped per line ~419 of runDetections.m). Uses default_SSR (120 nm, L-band 1.03 GHz per meta / 1.06 GHz on sensor object - see MSSR-F2) + default_crossing_pair targets + none terrain + horizon-masking ON. EXPECTED CONSOLE SIGNATURE: 'Primary sensors: 0 | Beacon sensors: 1', 'MSSR detected: SensorIndex=1', per-scan 'Primary=0, Beacon=N, total=N (clutter=0)'. EXPECTED WARNING (not a regression): 'Only 4 scan(s) - need at least 5.' The default_crossing_pair targets sit at 5000 m altitude with start ranges of 30-50 km, putting target elevation angles in the 5-11 degree range - above the SSR's narrow +3 degree upper elevation edge. Targets drop out of beam as they approach the tower, producing only 4 scans in 60 s instead of the expected 12. This is correct ASR-11 MSSR behavior (narrow elevation by design, for en-route transponder traffic, NOT overhead coverage) - see MSSR-F4 / X-F5 in SENSOR_VALIDATION_MATRIX.md. Sensor pipeline verification is unaffected: Gates 3, 4, and 6 all pass on this run. Full Tracked% validation needs a sensor-compatible target geometry and is out of scope for the sensor-correctness audit.
